articles.title: Who is Eryn Bonner? The Arizona State cheerleader who was brutally arrested by the police
articles.standfirst: ASU senior Eryn Bonner has become the focus of a viral police-arrest controversy after footage from July resurfaced, with prosecutors now pursuing misdemeanor charges
articles.summary: ASU senior Eryn Bonner has become the focus of a viral police-arrest controversy after footage from July resurfaced, with prosecutors now pursuing misdemeanor charges
articles.body:
E ryn Bonner , a 21-year-old Arizona State University senior and member of the school’s Stunt Devils, has found herself at the center of a growing controversy after video of her arrest in Tempe went viral.

The footage, recorded during an early-morning incident on July 19, shows Bonner approaching police officers who were attempting to detain another person on Mill Avenue. She had reportedly been told to move away from the officers before returning toward the confrontation.

“Let him go, let him go,” Bonner could be heard shouting shortly before the situation escalated.

An officer then pushed Bonner to the ground. Body-camera footage released by police shows the ensuing struggle, during which officers restrained her and she appears to be struck before eventually being placed in handcuffs. Bonner was reportedly left with bruises following the encounter.

Tempe police have offered a different account of what prompted the force. According to the department, Bonner interfered with the arrest and allegedly punched an officer multiple times. That allegation is central to the case now heading toward Tempe City Court.

Bonner is currently facing two misdemeanor charges: disorderly conduct and hindering or interfering with police.

The charges came after the Maricopa County Attorney’s Office declined to pursue felony allegations against her. Tempe subsequently moved forward with misdemeanor charges after reviewing the available evidence.

Who is Eryn Bonner and what is her connection to ASU?

Bonner is a senior at Arizona State and a member of the university’s Stunt Devils, a competitive program that combines athletic elements of cheerleading with head-to-head competition.

ASU describes STUNT as a sport built around partner stunts, pyramids and tosses, jumps, tumbling and team routines. The Stunt Devils compete as a club team and have been working to establish the sport as a larger presence within college athletics.

Bonner has also achieved recognition within the sport. The College STUNT Coaches Association listed her as a First Team All-American in its 2024 selections, highlighting her standing as an accomplished competitor before the arrest brought her name into the national spotlight.

The dispute surrounding the July incident has now extended beyond the criminal charges. Bonner's attorney, Benjamin Taylor , has strongly criticized the officers' actions and called for the officer involved to be fired.

“This was very extreme, very excessive and there was no need for double pushes, jumping on top and multiple strikes,” Taylor said. “The city of Tempe would be very vindictive to try to charge her again after they see what this officer did,” Taylor said.

Taylor has also raised concerns about what he described as inappropriate touching during the arrest.

“If you look at the end of the video, there’s some odd touching at the end of the video which is very concerning,” he said. “At the end you see his hand go on her buttocks which is very odd in this situation.”

Bonner's family has similarly condemned what they believe happened to her.

“There are no words to fully describe the heartbreak of watching our daughter being hurt by someone entrusted to protect and serve our community,” the Bonner family said.

“The hardest thing is seeing the pain and sadness in her eyes that we cannot take away,” the statement continued. “Expecting public servants to live up to the highest standards of their profession is not an act of animosity toward those who serve with honor.”

“Rather, it is essential to preserving public trust and upholding the integrity and legitimacy of our institutions. We respectfully ask for your prayers and support as our daughter and our family continue to heal.”

The case, however, does not have a single uncontested interpretation. Josh Logan , a former Chandler police officer and founder of Guardian Training and Consulting, said that if the officer's account that Bonner punched him is accurate, the use of force could fall within police policy.

“If you reach that level of active aggression, you’re within policy to perform closed fist strikes to the face,” Logan told the outlet.

At the same time, Logan questioned aspects of what can be seen in the footage, particularly the moment Bonner is thrown onto a bicycle during the struggle.

“There’s so many dangerous things on that bicycle that can cut and scrape. I have scars from cogwheels to chains and everything in between. It appears that she’s trying to move her off the bike and that happens in a split second in a very chaotic scene, and then they take her into custody and go from there,” Logan said.

The Tempe Police Department has said the incident remains under administrative review. The department has emphasized that the viral clip represents only part of a rapidly developing encounter and that investigators will examine the footage alongside the other available evidence.

“Consistent with our policies, this incident is currently under administrative review. The video of the incident, along with all other available evidence, will be carefully evaluated as part of that process,” the department told the outlet.

For Bonner , the controversy is now moving into two separate arenas: a criminal case involving two misdemeanor allegations and an internal review examining the conduct of the officers involved.

A pre-trial conference is scheduled for November 4 in Tempe Municipal Court, while the police review remains ongoing.

Until those processes are completed, the circumstances surrounding the arrest remain contested. What is clear is that a student who had previously been known primarily for her achievements with ASU's Stunt Devils has now become the central figure in a much wider debate over police intervention, use of force and accountability.

articles.title: How much can you earn while on Social Security and what does the SSA count as earnings?
articles.standfirst: Working while collecting Social Security is allowed, but your age and type of income can determine whether your benefits are reduced
articles.summary: Working while collecting Social Security is allowed, but your age and type of income can determine whether your benefits are reduced
articles.body:
Receiving Social Security retirement benefits does not automatically mean you have to stop working.

Millions of Americans continue earning wages after claiming benefits, but the Social Security Administration (SSA) applies an earnings test to people who have not yet reached full retirement age.

The important distinction is that the SSA does not count every dollar that comes into your household when determining whether your benefits should be withheld.

For 2026, someone who is collecting Social Security and remains below full retirement age for the entire year can earn up to $24,480 without triggering a reduction in benefits.

Once earnings exceed that threshold, the SSA withholds $1 in Social Security benefits for every $2 earned above the limit.

That does not mean the money is permanently lost. The SSA adjusts benefits once the beneficiary reaches full retirement age to account for months in which benefits were withheld because of the earnings test.

The rules become more generous in the calendar year someone reaches full retirement age. In 2026, the earnings threshold is $65,160, but the higher limit applies only to earnings received before the month the person reaches full retirement age.

The reduction is then $1 for every $3 earned above that amount. Beginning with the month full retirement age is reached, there is no earnings limit.

Full retirement age depends on a person's birth year, so beneficiaries should check their individual FRA rather than assuming it is the same for everyone.

What does the Social Security Administration count as earnings?

The definition of earnings is particularly important because some types of income that may look like wages for tax purposes do not count under the Social Security earnings test.

The SSA counts wages from employment and net earnings from self-employment. Wages can include salary, bonuses, commissions and vacation pay. For self-employed workers, the relevant figure is generally net earnings rather than gross business revenue.

Several other common sources of retirement income are excluded from the earnings test.

The SSA does not count pensions, annuities, investment income, interest, veterans benefits or other government or military retirement benefits when determining whether benefits should be withheld because of work.

That means someone could potentially receive income from investments or withdraw money from a retirement account while also working without those withdrawals being treated as earnings under the retirement earnings test.

For example, a retiree earning $20,000 from a job in 2026 would remain below the $24,480 earnings limit. A person earning $30,000 would be $5,520 above the threshold. Under the 1-for-2 rule, the SSA could withhold $2,760 in benefits.

However, the exact impact on an individual's payments can depend on when they work, when they claim benefits and whether they reach full retirement age during the year.

There is also a special monthly rule for some people who retire during the year. In 2026, someone below full retirement age can receive a full Social Security payment for a month in which they earn no more than $2,040, provided they meet the applicable requirements.

For someone reaching full retirement age during 2026, the corresponding monthly amount is $5,430 for months before reaching FRA.

Working can also have a positive long-term effect on Social Security . The SSA reviews earnings each year, and if a new year of work produces earnings higher than one of the lower years in a person's benefit calculation, the newer amount can replace it.

Because retirement benefits generally use a worker's highest 35 years of earnings, additional work can sometimes increase the eventual monthly benefit.

The key takeaway is that there is no universal income cap on working while receiving Social Security .

The $24,480 figure applies to beneficiaries who are below full retirement age throughout 2026, while people reaching FRA during the year face the higher $65,160 threshold before their FRA month. Once full retirement age arrives, the earnings test disappears.

Anyone whose expected earnings change after claiming benefits should notify the SSA, particularly if they are below full retirement age, to reduce the risk of unexpected benefit adjustments.

articles.standfirst: The Powerball jackpot has climbed to an estimated $467 million, with players across the country waiting for Monday night's winning numbers
articles.summary: The Powerball jackpot has climbed to an estimated $467 million, with players across the country waiting for Monday night's winning numbers
articles.body:
P owerball players have another major jackpot to chase on Monday, October 5, with an estimated $467 million prize up for grabs after the latest drawing failed to produce a jackpot winner.

The winning numbers for Monday night's drawing are not yet available as of the latest update. The drawing is scheduled for later Monday night, meaning players will need to wait until the numbers are selected before checking whether they hold a jackpot-winning ticket.

The official Powerball website lists the estimated jackpot at $467 million, with a cash value of $192.4 million for a winner who chooses the lump-sum option rather than the annuity.

Monday's jackpot has grown because nobody matched all five white balls and the red Powerball in Saturday's drawing.

The numbers drawn on Saturday, October 3, were 4, 42, 44, 55 and 59, with 14 selected as the Powerball . The Power Play multiplier was 2X.

There was no jackpot winner, according to the official Powerball results. One ticket did match all five white balls and won the standard $1 million second-tier prize. That ticket was sold in Arizona.

As a result, the jackpot has moved higher for the next drawing, continuing a run that has attracted increasing attention as the prize approaches half a billion dollars.

What time is the Powerball drawing on October 5?

Powerball drawings take place three times each week, on Monday, Wednesday and Saturday. The official drawing time is 10:59 p.m. ET, and the draw is conducted at the Florida Lottery draw studio in Tallahassee.

That means players should not expect the October 5 winning numbers to be available during the afternoon or early evening. The numbers will only become official once the drawing has taken place and the results have been recorded.

A standard Powerball play costs $2. Players select five white-ball numbers from 1 through 69 and one red Powerball number from 1 through 26. The Power Play option can increase certain non-jackpot prizes for an additional cost, depending on the ticket and jurisdiction.

The odds demonstrate just how difficult it is to win the top prize. A ticket has jackpot odds of approximately 1 in 292.2 million, meaning the enormous prize comes with an equally enormous challenge for players hoping to hit every number.

The $467 million advertised jackpot represents the annuity value. Under Powerball's standard structure, a jackpot winner can instead select the cash option, which is currently estimated at $192.4 million before applicable taxes.

Taxes would reduce the amount ultimately received by a jackpot winner. Federal income tax applies to lottery winnings, while state and local taxes can also vary depending on where the winning ticket was purchased and the winner's circumstances.

For anyone checking a ticket after Monday's drawing, matching the Powerball alone is enough to win a prize, although that prize is $4. Matching additional numbers can produce substantially larger payouts. The official Powerball prize structure should be used when determining the value of a particular ticket.

The previous drawing also demonstrated that players do not need to win the jackpot to take home a significant amount. Saturday produced a $1 million Match 5 winner in Arizona, while numerous other tickets won prizes at lower tiers.

For now, however, the main question remains unanswered: who will hold the ticket that matches all six numbers?

The official winning numbers for Monday, October 5, will be added after the drawing. Until then, the $467 million jackpot remains up for grabs, with a $192.4 million estimated cash alternative awaiting whoever gets every number right.

articles.title: Could pneumonic plague reach the United States? The alert arising from the possible outbreak coming from Russia
articles.standfirst: The emergence of suspected cases in Russia once again drew attention to one of the most severe forms of the plague. Is there really a risk that the disease could spread to the United States?
articles.summary: The emergence of suspected cases in Russia once again drew attention to one of the most severe forms of the plague. Is there really a risk that the disease could spread to the United States?
articles.body:
The death of a worker at an institute specializing in dangerous diseases triggered quarantines and contact tracing in Siberia. Russia is talking about pneumonia of unknown origin, while the United States is following the case closely.

The case raised health alerts inside and outside Russia. The woman, identified by international media as Darya Shipilova, died after developing rapidly progressing pneumonia , while hospitals in the region imposed restrictions and authorities began monitoring people who had been in contact with her.

Five hospitals in the Siberian region of Irkutsk went into quarantine and some 200 people were isolated following the death from possible pneumonic plague of the laboratory technician at the Anti-Plague Institute.

What is pneumonic plague and why is it a concern?

Pneumonic plague represents one of the most critical health threats worldwide due to its extreme aggressiveness and ability to spread. Unlike the bubonic variant, this form of the infection directly attacks the lungs and is transmitted from person to person through the air, via the droplets expelled when coughing or sneezing.

This characteristic makes it the only variant of the bacterium Yersinia pestis capable of triggering massive and rapid outbreaks, which raises alarms among international public health organizations.

The main factor of concern among the medical community is its fulminant progression and its fatality rate, which approaches 100% if not treated in time. With an incubation period that can be as short as 24 hours, initial symptoms such as high fever and coughing up blood rapidly progress to severe respiratory failure. Although the disease is completely curable with common antibiotics, the window for action is extremely narrow, requiring immediate medical diagnosis and treatment within the first 24 hours from the onset of the initial symptoms to guarantee the patient's survival.

Symptoms can appear quickly and include fever, weakness, headache, shortness of breath, and cough , which in more advanced cases may contain blood.

Could it reach the United States?

The existence of cases in another country does not automatically mean that the disease is on its way to the United States . For international spread to occur, certain conditions of transmission and exposure would have to be met.

In addition, plague is not a completely unknown disease in U.S. territory. Human cases have been recorded, especially in some areas of the western part of the country, although they are infrequent. This means that the bacterium exists, but not that there is currently a widespread epidemic.

Secretary of State, Marco Rubio, confirmed that Washington is monitoring the situation along with the CDC and other federal agencies. Rubio indicated that for the moment he does not believe there is cause for widespread alarm, although he assured that the case warrants attention while more data becomes known about what happened in Siberia.

The fact that explains why it remains a concern

The case involves an employee of the Anti-Plague Research Institute in Irkutsk , Siberia. Russian authorities claim that tests have not shown that her illness was related to the dangerous pathogens handled at the facility, and they have denied finding evidence of a laboratory accident despite reports circulating online. Contacts have been traced and placed under medical observation, and authorities reported on Monday that no other illnesses linked to the institute have been identified.

The news about the suspected cases in Russia raises a health concern that must be analyzed with caution: the risk of international spread should not be confused with the possibility of a serious disease making headlines again. Monitoring the cases and confirming their origin will be key to determining the true scope of the episode.

articles.title: Where did the russian plague infection come from? Two theories emerge
articles.standfirst: A Russian lab worker died after a suspected plague infection, but the biggest question remains unanswered.
articles.summary: A Russian lab worker died after a suspected plague infection, but the biggest question remains unanswered.
articles.body:
A Russian laboratory technician who worked in plague research died after becoming infected, while authorities are monitoring around 190 people who may have been exposed. According to a local report, the young woman may have contracted the disease after accidentally breaking a test tube containing the pathogen , although another version suggests the infection occurred outside the laboratory. Authorities have not confirmed either scenario.

Daria Shipilova , 28, worked as a technician at the Irkutsk anti-plague laboratory in eastern Siberia , a facility that handles rare diseases. According to the independent outlet People of Baikal , she may have accidentally broken a test tube containing pneumonic plague.

Shipilova was admitted on September 29 to a hospital in the nearby city of Shelekhov, thousands of miles east of Moscow , with pneumonia symptoms and was placed on a ventilator. She died two days later, according to The Moscow Times .

Quarantine and authorities’ response

On Saturday , 189 people who may have come into contact with her were placed under quarantine, including other employees at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute . Regional governor Igor Kobzev said authorities held an emergency meeting over the weekend to address the “particularly dangerous infection” inside the laboratory. So far, no one else has shown symptoms, he said.

Russia’s health watchdog, Rospotrebnadzor , said some of those placed under “anti-epidemic measures” tested positive for other illnesses, including colds or COVID-19 . The agency attributed Shipilova’s death to “pneumonia of unknown origin.” Details surrounding the case remain limited in a country with little press freedom.

Where did the infection come from?

There is currently no official answer. Two versions have emerged:

Laboratory accident: According to People of Baikal, Shipilova broke a test tube containing pneumonic plague and later became ill. It is the most striking theory, but it is based on a single report and has not been confirmed by authorities.

Infection during a trip: Russian outlet Mash reported that the technician became ill after returning from a work trip to the neighboring region of Buryatia, where a plague outbreak had previously been recorded.

The official explanation of “pneumonia of unknown origin” does not clarify the source of the infection, and until laboratory analysis or an official report is released, both theories remain possible.

How plague is normally transmitted

Plague is usually spread through the bites of infected fleas that live on rodents. The region has a history of cases: the last recorded plague infection in Russia occurred in 2016 in Altai , when a 10-year-old boy contracted the disease after slaughtering a marmot. In neighboring Mongolia, authorities identified 137 outbreaks in 2023 across 17 regions .

In this case, the disease is pneumonic plague, a form that can spread from person to person through respiratory droplets. Symptoms typically appear one to three days after exposure and can worsen rapidly. Without treatment, it can cause swelling, shortness of breath and chest pain, but it can be cured with antibiotics if treated quickly, according to the CDC.

The so-called Black Death killed between 75 million and 200 million people in the 14th century , including between 30% and 60% of Europe’s population.

articles.body:
D onald Trump has given the green light to the execution of Nidal Malik Hasan, the former U.S. Army major sentenced to death for carrying out one of the bloodiest attacks on a United States military base . That decision was confirmed by Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell, who announced that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth recommended execution by firing squad and that the U.S. president approved the measure .

Hasan was found guilty of the shooting that took place on November 5, 2009 at Fort Hood base in Texas. That day he opened fire on U.S. military personnel at an Army personnel processing center, causing the deaths of 13 people and also leaving 32 others injured .

According to the Pentagon, the then military psychiatrist , who held the rank of major, shouted "Allahu Akbar" while carrying out the attack , considered one of the most serious episodes suffered by the United States Armed Forces on national soil.

He was sentenced to death in 2013

Hasan was sentenced to death 13 years ago after being found guilty of thirteen counts of premeditated murder and 32 others of attempted premeditated murder . Since then, he has remained confined at the military prison in Fort Leavenworth , in Kansas. The massacre took place at the Fort Hood Soldier Readiness Center, a facility through which service members passed as they prepared to be deployed overseas or returned from missions.

Once Trump has made the determination, it will now be the Secretary of the Army who must set the date and place where the execution will be carried out, according to U.S. authorities. The decision represents a new step in a case that remains one of the most shocking episodes in the recent history of the United States Army.

articles.title: Costco travel deals and every other benefit you may not be taking advantage of with your membership
articles.standfirst: Travel deals, healthcare discounts and car-buying benefits are among the lesser-known ways Costco membership can save money
articles.summary: Travel deals, healthcare discounts and car-buying benefits are among the lesser-known ways Costco membership can save money
articles.body:
Most Costco members know the familiar routine of stocking up on groceries, filling the cart with household essentials and perhaps finishing the trip with something from the food court.

But the value of a membership extends well beyond the warehouse aisles. Costco offers members a wide range of services covering travel, vehicles, healthcare, entertainment and home projects.

Executive members can receive additional benefits, including an annual 2% Reward on eligible purchases and services. Some of the biggest potential savings can come from expenses members might never think to associate with Costco.

Costco Travel offers more than discounted hotels

Costco Travel includes vacation packages, cruises, individual hotel stays and other options, with some packages adding extras such as theme-park tickets, resort credits, waived fees, Costco Shop Cards or local activities.

The travel program also extends to rental cars. Members can compare rates from Alamo, Avis, Budget and Enterprise , while participating locations may allow an additional driver without the usual extra fee. Most reservations also avoid cancellation charges, giving travelers additional flexibility.

Entertainment is another lesser-known benefit. Costco sells discounted tickets to concerts, sporting events and attractions, including football, soccer, hockey and NASCAR . Tickets are generally delivered digitally through booking partner FEVO , although buyers should note that purchases are typically nonrefundable and cannot be resold.

Healthcare, pets and home projects can also bring savings

Members can access discounted prescription medications, Costco Optical and hearing services, while virtual appointments through Sesame are available for $29 with participating independent doctors. Costco also offers discounts connected to fertility treatments and medications.

Pet owners have their own set of potential benefits. Costco members can receive discounts on Figo pet insurance, access virtual veterinary services through AskVet and use the Costco Member Prescription Program for eligible pet medications, with some prescriptions discounted by as much as 40%.

Homeowners may also find value through Costco’s installation and remodeling services. Available projects include flooring, bathrooms, countertops, custom closets, windows, HVAC systems and water filtration, with some purchases qualifying for Costco Shop Cards .

Your membership can help with cars and insurance

Costco’s Auto Program offers prearranged pricing on new and used vehicles through approved dealers, reducing the need for traditional dealership negotiation.

Members can also receive 15% off eligible parts through participating service centers, while Costco Tire Center purchases include installation and lifetime services such as balancing, rotation, inflation and flat-tire repair.

Insurance, phone-plan promotions, grocery delivery and bottled-water delivery add even more possibilities. The biggest takeaway is that members who only use Costco for shopping may be leaving significant value on the table.

articles.title: Jim Bakker cause of death: How did the controversial 86-year-old televangelist, who was embroiled in sexual and financial scandals, die?
articles.summary: Jim Bakker spent decades moving between religious celebrity, public disgrace and an unlikely broadcasting comeback. His death at 86 closes one of the most turbulent careers in modern American televangelism.
articles.body:
Jim Bakker spent decades moving between religious celebrity, public disgrace and an unlikely broadcasting comeback. His death at 86 closes one of the most turbulent careers in modern American televangelism.

His wife, Lori Bakker , announced that he died Monday night, describing him as a pioneer of Christian television and her “husband, my best friend, and the man I was honored to walk beside through so many seasons of life and ministry.”

No official cause of death has been announced. That uncertainty is significant because Bakker had suffered a serious stroke in 2020, an episode his wife described at the time as “the most vicious attack that he has ever experienced.”

He later acknowledged that the stroke had been more severe than first understood and said it had affected his memory.

Bakker remained focused on television

Despite those health concerns, Bakker continued to promote his ministry and television work.

His final Instagram post came on August 23, about six weeks before his death, when he celebrated the return of The Jim Bakker Show to the Impact Network.

Earlier this year, he also made an urgent appeal to viewers for donations, saying the ministry needed roughly $1 million to remain on the air.

“I believe if everyone who watches this program will give a thousand dollars, we'll be able to pay our bills and stay on the air,” Bakker said. “Otherwise, we’ve got about another month, I don’t know, to stay on the air.”

That appeal underscored how closely his identity remained tied to broadcasting, even in his mid-80s.

Rise and fall reshaped American televangelism

Bakker became nationally famous in the 1970s alongside his first wife, Tammy Faye Bakker , through The PTL Club. Their ministry eventually expanded into Heritage USA, a massive Christian theme park and resort in South Carolina.

At its peak, Bakker ’s television operation reportedly reached millions of homes and generated enormous sums of money. That empire unraveled in the late 1980s amid sex and financial scandals.

Bakker was later convicted on fraud-related charges and served prison time from 1989 to 1994. He eventually returned to religious television with Lori, launching The Jim Bakker Show from Missouri and rebuilding a smaller but still devoted audience.

His son, pastor Jay Bakker , offered a more complicated reflection after his death.

“He was also my father and a grandfather and I need to mourn in my own time,” Jay Bakker wrote, adding: “I need the freedom to feel anger and feel loss.”

Until the family releases more information, the exact cause of Bakker’s death remains unknown.

articles.title: Delta plane clips Air Canada jet at LAX before Tokyo flight, prompting FAA investigation
articles.standfirst: A startling scene that leaves questions unanswered
articles.summary: A startling scene that leaves questions unanswered
articles.body:
A Delta Air Lines plane preparing to depart for Tokyo struck part of an Air Canada aircraft at Los Angeles International Airport on Tuesday , October 6, prompting a Federal Aviation Administration investigation. The incident happened around 10:30 a.m. local time, while both aircraft were on the ground.

Delta identified its aircraft as an Airbus A350-900 carrying 275 passengers and 15 crew members , according to a spokesperson quoted by Fox News. Air Canada separately confirmed that no passengers or crew members were reported injured.

Air Canada’s plane had landed safely and was being towed to its gate

According to the FAA’s preliminary account, Delta Flight 7 was taxiing for departure when its left wingtip clipped the horizontal stabilizer of Air Canada Flight 785 the horizontal surface on the aircraft’s tail. The Air Canada plane was being towed and had stopped short of its gate. The agency has not announced a cause or assigned responsibility.

An Air Canada spokesperson told CityNews that Flight AC785 had arrived from Toronto and landed safely before the contact occurred during its transfer to the gate. The airline said the aircraft would be taken out of service for inspection and repairs. For its passengers, the disruption came after the airborne portion of their journey was already complete.

Delta also acknowledged the incident and apologized for the disruption. “We apologize to our customers for the experience and delay in their travel,” the airline said in a statement reported by Fox News.

The FAA’s initial statement establishes which aircraft made contact and where the impact occurred, but leaves the circumstances leading to the collision unresolved. Those questions remain part of the investigation, while Air Canada’s aircraft awaits inspection and repairs.

articles.title: Woman interrupts marriage proposal and shouts “Go back to Mexico” in Laguna Beach
articles.standfirst: Emmanuel Banuelos had spent weeks planning his proposal to Hayley Lugos, but a woman approached just before he could pop the question, and the situation ended up going viral.
articles.summary: Emmanuel Banuelos had spent weeks planning his proposal to Hayley Lugos, but a woman approached just before he could pop the question, and the situation ended up going viral.
articles.body:
Proposing to someone means imagining that moment over and over again. What to say, when to do it and how to make sure everything goes the way you planned. For Emmanuel Banuelos, that moment finally arrived on October 2 in Laguna Beach, California , but an unexpected interruption completely changed what he had prepared.

Banuelos was with Hayley Lugos at Crescent Bay Point Park, where the couple had gone for the proposal. Hayley’s sister, Trinity, was recording when a woman walking her dog approached them and began confronting them for using the park . She told them the area was for people who lived there and claimed the police were on their way because they did not have permission to be there.

The mariachis began playing, and Emmanuel and Hayley walked toward the spot they had chosen for the moment, while the woman continued confronting the group. That was when she made the comment that took the confrontation to another level: “This isn’t Mexico either, you m*********, go back to Mexico!”***

Emmanuel did not hide how deeply those words affected him. The young man explained that he has deep Mexican roots , which made hearing that comment particularly painful as he was preparing to ask Hayley to marry him. She also said she was saddened by what happened .

But the confrontation did not change the answer Emmanuel had gone there hoping to hear. The proposal eventually happened, and the couple got engaged. They later returned to Ontario, where he organized a surprise party to celebrate the news with their loved ones .

articles.title: Christa Pike is awake after failed execution as her attorneys seek more information
articles.standfirst: Pike somehow survived two lethal injection doses.
articles.summary: Pike somehow survived two lethal injection doses.
articles.body:
Death row inmate Christa Pike has regained consciousness after Tennessee’s failed attempt to execute her by lethal injection last week, and her attorneys are set to head to court Wednesday to seek more information about what went wrong.

Pike, 50, survived two doses of pentobarbital as executioners attempted to put her to death Sept. 30 for the 1995 beating and stabbing death of classmate Colleen Slemmer . Pike is believed to be the only person to survive after lethal injection drugs were administered.

Pike’s attorneys are set to appear in court Wednesday as they are seeking more information from the Tennessee Department of Correction. Chancery Court Judge I’Ashea Myles has scheduled a Wednesday morning status conference in Nashville in the case.

“ Against all odds, Christa Pike is conscious, speaking, and continues to receive critical medical care ,” attorneys for Pike said in a statement. Pike’s prognosis remains unclear and, at a minimum, she faces a lengthy recovery, the attorneys said. They said Pike's arms were burned and blistered after the attempted lethal injection and that she is handcuffed to the hospital bed.

Pike’s attorneys are seeking a court order to require the prison system to preserve information from the attempted execution including drug lot numbers, needles, execution logs and other information.

Attorneys with the Tennessee attorney general’s office wrote in a Tuesday court filing that the court order is unnecessary because the prison system is “ obliged to maintain this evidence in other cases and must assure it is preserved .” They said state officials have taken “ the necessary steps to obtain medical care for Pike and ascertain what occurred .”

Republican Gov. Bill Lee called what happened “deeply disturbing” and ordered a “ comprehensive, third-party review to determine exactly what occurred .” The governor postponed the state’s only other execution scheduled for this year.

Medical and lethal injection experts have focused on the possibility that a problem with the IV line caused the drug to pool in her tissue rather than entering her bloodstream. Pike’s attorneys wrote in their court filing that “ apparently at no point did any member of the execution team realize that the IV lines were not correctly placed or that the veins had blown .”

The attempted execution got underway around 7:30 p.m. on Sept. 30 when Pike was given a chance to make a final statement. About five minutes later, Pike raised her head and said her arm was hurting. At some point she appeared to lose consciousness, but she could be heard audibly breathing until media were escorted from the witness room at 8:53 p.m. An ambulance arrived at the prison at 9:14 p.m. to take Pike to a hospital.

articles.title: Who’s getting the $90 Medicare Improvement Fund rebate check? Eligibility and when you’ll get it
articles.standfirst: More than 20 million people are eligible, but Medicare Advantage members and several other groups are excluded
articles.summary: More than 20 million people are eligible, but Medicare Advantage members and several other groups are excluded
articles.body:
Millions of Americans are receiving an unfamiliar $90 deposit this week, and the payment isn't a new Social Security benefit.

It's a one-time Medicare Improvement Fund rebate tied to Part B coverage, and most eligible beneficiaries are expected to receive it automatically around October 8.

The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services says 20.8 million people qualify for the payment. That is roughly one-third of Medicare Part B’s approximately 62.9 million enrollees, leaving about 40 million people outside the program.

The rebate comes as Medicare costs continue to rise, with Part B premiums increasing by more than $200 annually in 2026 and projected to climb again in 2027.

Who qualifies for $90 Medicare rebate?

Eligibility is limited to people enrolled in Original Medicare Part B who live in the United States and meet two additional conditions.

They cannot be receiving Medicaid assistance to help pay their Medicare premiums, and they cannot be paying an Income-Related Monthly Adjustment Amount , or IRMAA. Beneficiaries enrolled in Medicare Advantage don't qualify.

That means the excluded groups include Medicare Advantage members , higher-income beneficiaries who pay income-related premiums, people receiving Medicaid premium assistance and beneficiaries who do not live in the United States.

Juliette Cubanski , vice president and director of the Program on Medicare Policy at KFF, said the income restriction reflects the administration’s view that wealthier beneficiaries may be better positioned to handle higher costs.

“People who are paying the income-related premium have higher incomes to begin with, so the thinking is that they may be better able to absorb higher costs and wouldn’t benefit as much from the $90 payment as people with lower incomes,” Cubanski told CBS News.

When will $90 payment arrive?

Most eligible beneficiaries will receive the money by direct deposit from the Social Security Administration on or around October 8.

People who don't receive their benefits by direct deposit will instead get a paper check from the U.S. Department of the Treasury later in October.

That check will include the message: “Medicare Improvement Fund Payment; $90 Payment to Offset October Premium.”

CMS has said most people don't need to apply or take any action to receive the money. Beneficiaries who are unsure whether they qualify can call 1-800-MEDICARE at 1-800-633-4227.

Anyone who believes they are eligible but has not received the payment can contact the Social Security Administration at 1-800-772-1213 beginning October 15 to check its status.

The rebate is small compared with the broader rise in Medicare costs, but for those who qualify, it should arrive automatically.

The most important distinction is that the payment is aimed at eligible Original Medicare Part B beneficiaries, not everyone enrolled in Medicare.

articles.title: How much will your Social Security increase next year with the Trump Bump after the last estimate?
articles.standfirst: Current forecasts point towards 3.5% to 3.6% increase, but September inflation could still push benefits higher
articles.summary: Current forecasts point towards 3.5% to 3.6% increase, but September inflation could still push benefits higher
articles.body:
The final number that will shape Social Security checks throughout 2027 is almost here, and current estimates suggest beneficiaries could receive their biggest cost-of-living adjustment in several years.

The Senior Citizens League and independent Social Security analyst Mary Johnson currently project a 3.5% COLA, while AARP has put its estimate slightly higher at 3.6%. At 3.5%, the average monthly Social Security benefit would rise by approximately $67.90, from $1,940.08 to about $2,007.98.

That estimate isn't locked in. September’s inflation data remains the final piece of the calculation, leaving open the possibility that next year’s increase comes in slightly higher.

Why 2027 Social Security increase could still grow

Social Security ’s annual COLA is determined using the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers, or CPI-W.

The Social Security Administration compares the average CPI-W reading from July through September with the equivalent period one year earlier. September’s figure therefore has the ability to move the final percentage.

President Donald Trump doesn't set the COLA, despite the increase sometimes being described as a “Trump bump.”

His administration’s economic policies can, however, influence some of the conditions feeding into inflation. Higher energy costs and tariffs have both been cited as factors capable of increasing prices for businesses and consumers.

TSCL executive director Shannon Benton said short-term changes remain the biggest variable heading into the announcement.

“The biggest thing we’re watching with the COLA announcement coming are short-term shocks to the economy that push inflation way up or down in the next 30 days,” Benton said.

Bigger COLA doesn't mean retirees are better off

A larger Social Security increase sounds like straightforward good news, but COLAs rise because living costs have already increased.

Beneficiaries absorb those higher prices before the adjustment reaches their checks in January. That means retirees dealing with more expensive fuel, groceries or healthcare now must wait months before benefits catch up.

There is also an ongoing debate over whether the CPI-W accurately reflects the spending patterns of older Americans, particularly their healthcare costs.

The Senior Citizens League found in its 2026 Senior Survey that 89% of older Americans believed that year’s COLA had failed to keep pace with inflation.

AARP has also highlighted the pressure higher prices are placing on household budgets. Survey data from the Nationwide Retirement Institute found that 74% of Social Security recipients had adjusted their finances because inflation was outpacing benefit increases.

The wait for the final figure will not last much longer. September’s Consumer Price Index report is scheduled for October 14, with the Social Security Administration expected to announce the official 2027 COLA shortly afterward.

A 3.5% increase remains the central estimate. If September inflation comes in stronger than expected, beneficiaries could see an even larger adjustment, although that would also reflect higher prices they are already paying.

articles.standfirst: Monday produced no grand-prize winner, setting up another huge drawing
articles.summary: Monday produced no grand-prize winner, setting up another huge drawing
articles.body:
The Powerball jackpot is back in the spotlight after Monday night failed to produce a grand-prize winner, sending the top prize climbing to an estimated $485 million for Wednesday, October 7.

The cash option for the drawing is approximately $199.8 million, before federal and any applicable state taxes. Wednesday’s winning numbers haven't yet been drawn.

The drawing is scheduled for 10:59 p.m. ET, with results expected shortly afterward. Monday’s winning numbers were 16, 23, 32, 36 and 54, with a Powerball of 9 and a 2x Power Play. No ticket matched all six numbers.

What are the Powerball winning numbers for October 7?

The official winning numbers for Wednesday night will be announced after the drawing takes place.

Winning numbers : To be announced

Powerball : To be announced

Power Play : To be announced

Powerball drawings are held three times a week — Monday, Wednesday and Saturday — giving players regular chances to chase the growing jackpot.

A standard ticket costs $2, and players select five white-ball numbers plus one red Powerball . The prize structure means a ticket does not need to match all six numbers to win something.

Matching only the Powerball is worth $4, while matching one white ball plus the Powerball also pays $4. The prizes increase as more numbers are matched, with five white balls normally worth $1 million.

How much would the winner actually receive?

The advertised $485 million jackpot reflects the annuity option, which is paid over a period of years. A winner can instead choose the one-time cash option of about $199.8 million, which is the amount available before taxes.

That difference is significant, but both options would still represent a life-changing payout.

Monday’s rollover also produced plenty of smaller winners. In California alone, tens of thousands of tickets won prizes, although nobody claimed the jackpot.

The absence of a grand-prize winner means Wednesday’s drawing will carry even more attention.

Powerball jackpot continues to build momentum

Powerball has produced some enormous jackpots in recent years, including prizes well above $1 billion.

The current $485 million pot is still some distance from those records, but another rollover would push it even higher heading into the weekend.

Players holding tickets should check their numbers after the drawing and confirm any potential winnings through an official state lottery or Powerball source.

Until then, the biggest question remains simple. Will Wednesday finally produce a jackpot winner, or will the prize grow again?

articles.title: A american diver volunteered to clean trash from a lake: he discovered a 1,000-year-old dugout canoe at the bottom
articles.standfirst: The expert makes a discovery that would correspond to indigenous communities of Milwaukee
articles.summary: The expert makes a discovery that would correspond to indigenous communities of Milwaukee
articles.body:
Human beings continue to find new r emains belonging to very ancient times that demonstrate the evolution of life on Earth. One of the most surprising is the work of Mark Schachtnet , a diver who had volunteered to clean Lake Pewaukee, in Wisconsin (United States) . While exploring the bottom, the expert came across an elongated object that looked like a simple canoe.

What appeared to be a simple vessel , possibly sunk by some kind of accident during an excursion, turned out to be a canoe hundreds of years old and an example of how the most legendary civilizations moved around and created their own means of transportation.

Experts from the Wisconsin Historical Society, after an exhaustive analysis and study, have determined that it is a dugout canoe about 1,000 years old , handmade and used by the indigenous communities of what is now Milwaukee between the 10th and 11th centuries .

An unusual canoe in good condition

According to estimates, it is the first canoe of this style discovered in Lake Pewaukee, since previous finds occurred in other areas such as, for example, Lake Mendota. The study revealed that it is a well-preserved canoe, 5.26 meters long and 0.55 meters wide , with walls just over six centimeters thick and a bottom about 12 centimeters thick.

Schachtnet, on May 6, had no doubt that it was an unusual canoe when he approached it and examined it closely. After finding it, he reported it to Tamara Thomsen , an archaeologist with the aforementioned association. “I’m always on the lookout. There usually aren’t any large logs around there, unless it’s some kind of shelter for fish. All of that was very obvious ,” the diver told the Wisconsin State Journal.

articles.title: SSA COLA 2027 Update: Release date, latest changes and everything to know before it's announced
articles.summary: Retirees will soon know exactly how much their Social Security payments are set to rise in 2027.
articles.body:
Retirees will soon know exactly how much their Social Security payments are set to rise in 2027.

The Social Security Administration is scheduled to announce the official cost-of-living adjustment on October 14, following the release of the final inflation data needed to calculate the increase.

That number matters because it determines how much monthly Social Security benefits will increase next year.

The adjustment is based on the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers , known as CPI-W. The SSA compares the average CPI-W reading from the third quarter of the current year with the same period from the last year in which a COLA took effect.

If there is an increase, it's rounded to the nearest tenth of a percentage point.

Latest estimates point to mid-3% increase

Recent forecasts suggest the 2027 COLA could land in the mid-3% range.

The Senior Citizens League has projected a 3.6% increase, which would translate to about $69.75 more per month for the average beneficiary if that estimate holds.

Independent Social Security and Medicare analyst Mary Johnson has offered a slightly lower projection of 3.4%. Those estimates have moved around during the year as inflation changed direction.

“One of the biggest challenges this year has been the sharp swings in inflation,” TSCL executive director Shannon Benton said. “It started at 2.2% in January, climbed to 4.4% in May, then fell to 3.5% in June.”

She added: “Fortunately, our model is designed not to overreact to these swings, keeping our COLA projections relatively steady.”

Earlier projections had climbed as high as 3.8%.

Why final September inflation number matters

The COLA is based specifically on July, August and September CPI-W data, which makes the final monthly reading especially important. A stronger September inflation figure could push the final adjustment slightly higher, while a softer number could pull it lower.

That makes October 14 the key date for beneficiaries. The broader economic picture remains mixed. Job growth has slowed, unemployment has ticked higher and inflation is still above the Federal Reserve’s 2% target.

Higher energy costs and persistent consumer prices have continued to pressure household budgets, particularly for retirees who depend heavily on fixed income.

COLA not the only Social Security update

The October announcement is also expected to include several other program changes for 2027. Those can include updated earnings limits, taxable wage thresholds and other figures affecting workers and beneficiaries.

That means the announcement isn't just about how much checks will rise. It will also provide a clearer picture of how Social Security rules will change for people still working, those already receiving benefits and those preparing to retire.

The headline figure will remain the COLA. Based on current estimates, beneficiaries should expect something around 3.4% to 3.6%, with the official number arriving on October 14.

articles.title: Outcry over the photo of Donald Trump in a cheap suit and, probably, made in China
articles.standfirst: Society is thinking about the tariff policy that the president is pursuing
articles.summary: Society is thinking about the tariff policy that the president is pursuing
articles.body:
"Public figures" usually always wear the best brands . Many times this is even the case when they do not want to, since for reasons of protocol this is mandatory. However, it is surprising when one of these public figures wears an outfit that is not tailor-made by a major brand or that is even low-cost.

This is accentuated when it is Donald Trump , the President of the United States and one of the most influential people in the world, who has been identified wearing a suit from a brand that could be considered ‘low cost’.

This photo taken of the President suggests a suit from the Traveler collection , according to CNN. These separate suit pieces from Jos A. Bank are selling for $279, in the size and color worn by Donald Trump.

It should be noted that neither Trump nor his family are going through financial difficulties since, for example, their family company has seen its cryptocurrency investments generate profits of more than 1 billion, according to financial reports.

Some people think that this move is a strategy to bring the President of the United States closer to the people, a strategy seen before with other presidents such as Al Gore's sweaters, John Kerry's camouflage hunting jacket, or even George H. W. Bush's cowboy boots.

Donald Trump's suit from Jos. A. Bank is imported

Not only that, but the Jos. A. Bank brand is characterized by importing a large part of its products from countries such as China or Bangladesh, although it has not been confirmed that this clothing is among the imported items and it may have been made on American soil.

This clashes radically with Donald Trump's policy of imposing steep tariffs on foreign products to promote domestic goods at the expense of imports.

articles.standfirst: Rachel is expected to weaken before reaching northern Baja California, but dangerous surf, coastal flooding and weekend rain remain concerns for Southern California
articles.summary: Rachel is expected to weaken before reaching northern Baja California, but dangerous surf, coastal flooding and weekend rain remain concerns for Southern California
articles.body:
For Southern California residents watching Hurricane Rachel, the first danger is already reaching the shoreline. Swells from the distant storm are creating hazardous beach conditions as forecasters track an expected sharp turn toward the northeast later this week. Rachel is forecast to weaken along the way, but its changing course has put the region’s weekend weather under closer watch.

The National Weather Service’s Thursday morning forecast points to landfall in northern Baja California late Saturday night , with Rachel expected to fall below tropical storm strength before reaching land. Its interaction with a separate low-pressure system could spread tropical moisture into Southern California , bringing showers from late Saturday night through Sunday night. The forecast therefore calls for impacts from a weakening system rather than a hurricane striking California at full strength.

Rachel’s weakening winds do not end the coastal threat

Beach alerts now cover both San Diego and Orange counties . An advisory issued Thursday calls for surf of 3 to 5 feet, with sets reaching 7 feet, alongside dangerous rip currents. A beach hazards statement remains in effect through Friday evening, while a coastal flood advisory extends until 2 p.m. PDT Tuesday, October 13. articles.title: Who was Phoenix Phillips? The fan that went to watch Steelers vs Browns and ended up dead, floating in the Cuyahoga River
articles.standfirst: The 24-year-old father vanished in Cleveland before authorities recovered his body
articles.summary: The 24-year-old father vanished in Cleveland before authorities recovered his body
articles.body:
Phoenix Phillips had traveled from Perryville, Maryland, to Cleveland for the matchup between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cleveland Browns , but the football weekend took a devastating turn when he vanished in the city.

His disappearance quickly became a serious concern for local authorities and missing-person organizations. Cleveland police described the case as “concerning” as the search intensified and Phillips ’ family waited for any sign that he might be found safe.

That search ended with tragic news when emergency crews responded to a report of a person in the Cuyahoga River near Jacobs Pavilion. A body was recovered from the water at around 1 p.m. and later identified as Phillips.

Who was Phoenix Phillips?

Phillips was a 24-year-old father from Perryville, a Maryland community northeast of Baltimore. He had made the trip to Ohio specifically to attend the Steelers-Browns rivalry game before disappearing in downtown Cleveland.

Cleveland Missing , a nonprofit organization involved in raising awareness about his disappearance, worked to publicize the search while his relatives waited for answers about where he had gone.

Before authorities confirmed his death, Cleveland Missing social worker Breejanee Alford said she had met with Phillips ’ family during the search. She described them as “devastated” and said they remembered him as a “loving dad.”

Those words have become central to the story because the circumstances initially focused attention on a football trip gone wrong. To his family, however, Phillips was a young father whose disappearance turned an ordinary weekend away into a nightmare.

Authorities still don't know how he died

The biggest question in the case remains unanswered. Officials have not publicly explained how Phillips died or how he came to be in the Cuyahoga River after disappearing in Cleveland .

No confirmed cause of death has been released, and authorities have not said whether they believe an accident, foul play or another explanation was involved in the circumstances surrounding his death.

That leaves investigators with the difficult task of reconstructing Phillips’ final movements and determining what happened between the time he disappeared and the discovery of his body near Jacobs Pavilion.

The recovery of Phillips ’ body brought an end to the search itself, but it did not bring clarity to the events that led to his death or provide the answers his family is still seeking.

A football trip that became family tragedy

Phillips ’ case has drawn national attention because of the heartbreaking sequence of events surrounding his visit to Cleveland. He traveled for an NFL rivalry game, disappeared in an unfamiliar city and was later found dead in the river.

The football connection may explain why the story spread so widely, but it does not define who Phillips was. He was 24 years old, a father and someone his family described as deeply loved.

Until investigators establish what happened, his relatives are left with the hardest kind of uncertainty. They now know where the search ended, but they still do not know why it ended there.

articles.title: She survived and is furious: Christa Pike's legal team just revealed her true condition following failed execution
articles.standfirst: The 50-year-old is conscious and mobile, but concerns remain over severe arm injuries and possible brain damage
articles.summary: The 50-year-old is conscious and mobile, but concerns remain over severe arm injuries and possible brain damage
articles.body:
Christa Pike remains in critical care more than a week after the failed lethal injection, but her attorneys say her condition has improved enough for her to move around on her own for short periods.

Attorney Stephen Ferrell said Pike’s recovery has been uneven, with encouraging physical progress alongside serious injuries and lingering cognitive problems.

“She is up and walking for the first time today, but just around the room, not very far,” Ferrell told the BBC.

He also said Pike’s arms remain badly injured and that she is still struggling to use them normally after the execution attempt.

Pike is awake, but her lawyers say she remains mentally ‘foggy’

Ferrell described Pike’s mental condition as a mixture of progress and concern, saying she is alert enough to communicate but not yet functioning normally.

“Good that she is fairly with it, but she’s also somewhat foggy,” he said. “She can lose her train of thought really easily and forgets where she’s going.”

Her legal team has said it is still too early to know whether Pike suffered any permanent brain damage during the execution attempt.

Attorney Randall Spivey said one thing is already clear: Pike understands what happened to her.

“She is angry and confused about everything right now,” Spivey told reporters. “She is very aware that the state tried to execute her.”

Pike’s attorneys allege that officials used at least seven needles while administering two doses of pentobarbital, with one needle reportedly emerging from her arm bent at a 90-degree angle.

Her legal team has also criticized the fact that she remains restrained in the hospital despite what they describe as extensive damage to both arms.

“Despite the severe damage she endured to her arms, she is still handcuffed and shackled to the bed,” her attorneys said.

“Her recovery is medically unprecedented. Her prognosis remains unclear but, at a minimum, we expect a long recovery.”

A judge has since ordered Tennessee officials to preserve syringes and other evidence connected to the execution attempt as questions continue over exactly what happened inside the death chamber.

An unprecedented legal situation is now taking shape

Pike had been scheduled to become the first woman executed in Tennessee in more than 200 years, but instead became the first prisoner in the United States known to survive a lethal injection attempt.

She was sentenced to death for the 1995 torture and murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer , a crime committed when Pike was 18.

The immediate focus now is not on the sentence itself, but on Pike’s recovery, the injuries she sustained and the legal consequences of an execution attempt that did not end in death.

She is conscious, mobile and still hospitalized.

According to her lawyers, she also remembers enough to know exactly what the state intended to do.

articles.title: Susan Dell's appearance goes viral after her visit to the White House: a striking physical transformation
articles.standfirst: Susan Dell's latest public appearance has sent social media into a frenzy over her dramatically different look
articles.summary: Susan Dell's latest public appearance has sent social media into a frenzy over her dramatically different look
articles.body:
Susan Dell's appearance at the White House has become an unexpected social media talking point after the philanthropist joined her husband, Dell Technologies founder Michael Dell , and President Donald Trump in the Oval Office on October 7.

The couple was at the White House to promote Trump Accounts, an investment initiative designed to give American children a financial start. The White House said nearly 70 million accounts had been created, including more than 60 million through automatic enrollment.

Eligible newborns can receive a $1,000 government contribution, while families and outside donors can add money under the program's rules.

Susan spoke during the appearance and encouraged parents and grandparents to make sure their children and grandchildren claim their accounts.

Michael Dell also confirmed that their previously announced $6.25 billion commitment was being distributed, with $250 contributions earmarked for 25 million children. He said more than 10 million accounts had received the money as of October 7, with the commitment expected to be funded by the end of the week.

However, photographs and video from the event quickly shifted the online conversation away from the initiative and toward Susan's appearance. Posts on X and other platforms scrutinized her facial expressions, makeup, gestures and overall appearance.

Some users speculated about possible cosmetic procedures, while others commented on her apparent weight and compared current photographs with older pictures.

Why Susan Dell's appearance became the story

The reaction isn't entirely new. Online discussions about changes in Susan's appearance have circulated for months, including a Reddit post that attracted attention in July.

Following her White House appearance, the conversation gained fresh momentum as users shared photographs and clips while debating how her look may have changed over the years.

Some social media users also connected the discussion to the phrase "Mar-a-Lago face," an expression used online to describe a particular polished or visibly altered aesthetic that some people associate with Trump's social circle.

Away from the viral discussion, Susan has a substantial public profile of her own. She and Michael Dell married in 1989 and have four children. She co-founded the Michael & Susan Dell Foundation in 1999 and serves as its board chair, helping oversee initiatives involving education, health care, employment and financial opportunity.

Her philanthropic work has included major support for health-care and education projects, while her family's latest commitment is tied directly to the children's investment program promoted at the White House.

The October 7 appearance was intended to spotlight children's financial accounts and encourage families to participate, however the online reaction shows how quickly attention surrounding a public figure can shift.

articles.title: How will El Niño affect winter weather in the US and which states could see the biggest changes?
articles.standfirst: NOAA’s October update points to a strengthening El Niño through early 2027
articles.summary: NOAA’s October update points to a strengthening El Niño through early 2027
articles.body:
For families planning holiday travel or getting their homes ready for winter, the latest El Niño forecast offers an early signal of what could be ahead. Southern states face increased odds of wetter conditions, while much of the northern United States leans toward a warmer season. Those shifts matter, but they do not tell residents when the next storm will arrive or whether their neighborhood will flood.

In its October 8 update , NOAA’s Climate Prediction Center said El Niño continues to strengthen, with a greater than 83% chance of strong-to-very-strong conditions through January–March 2027 . The agency also said the chances remain high for an event that could exceed the strength of previous El Niño episodes dating back to 1950. That remains a forecast, rather than a record already established. A potentially historic event makes preparation worthwhile; it does not guarantee historic weather in every state.

What El Niño could mean for your winter and what to do now

El Niño is a recurring climate pattern involving unusually warm water in the tropical Pacific and associated changes in atmospheric circulation. Its influence can shift the odds of seasonal temperature and precipitation patterns far beyond the ocean. NOAA cautions that even a powerful event does not guarantee the familiar El Niño effects everywhere.

For drivers, the most useful preparation is a plan for bad conditions. Before a winter trip, the National Weather Service recommends checking the vehicle’s lights, heater, windshield wipers and fluid levels . Carry blankets, water, nonperishable food, a flashlight and a phone charger. Check your state’s road conditions before leaving, and let someone know your route and expected arrival time. A broad outlook should not replace the forecast along your actual journey.

For households, prepare for the disruption a single storm can cause. Keep essential prescriptions, food, water, batteries and supplies for children and pets available. Test smoke and carbon monoxide detectors, and make sure everyone knows how to receive emergency information if the power goes out. The National Weather Service also warns that generators must never be operated in enclosed spaces.

In areas expecting more rain, flooded roads deserve particular attention. Water can hide damaged pavement, and its force is easy to underestimate. The National Weather Service says just 12 inches of rushing water can carry away most cars. Never drive around flood barriers or attempt to cross a flooded road because another vehicle made it through. Turn around and find a safe alternative.

The snowfall question remains more complicated than “wet” or “warm.” NOAA’s outlook discussed here does not provide a snowfall total for New York City, Chicago or Boston. More precipitation does not automatically mean more snow, and a warmer seasonal average does not describe every cold spell. City-specific snowfall estimates from private forecasters should be identified as their projections, rather than attributed to NOAA.

articles.title: Pentagon announces public livestream for execution of Fort Hood mass shooter
articles.standfirst: Pete Hegseth says the public will be able to watch Nidal Hasan’s firing squad execution, scheduled for December 3.
articles.summary: Pete Hegseth says the public will be able to watch Nidal Hasan’s firing squad execution, scheduled for December 3.
articles.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said Thursday that the public will be able to watch the firing squad execution of Nidal Hasan , a former Army officer convicted of the mass shooting at Fort Hood, Texas .

In an interview aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln with conservative media outlet Real America’s Voice, Hegseth said Hasan “going to get a firing squad of soldiers, and we’ll make sure that people are able to watch it.”

“People need to understand that there are serious consequences for these types of things,” Hegseth said, calling the execution method a “no-brainer.”

According to Hegseth , the execution will take place at 1 p.m. on December 3 at Fort Hood, on the same day of the week and at the same time of day as Hasan’s attack.

A Defense Department official said the execution will be livestreamed, although it remains unclear which platform will carry it.

An execution method not used in decades

The last military execution took place in 1961 , when Army Private John Bennett was hanged after being convicted of raping and attempting to murder an 11-year-old girl in Austria .

The last firing squad execution carried out by the U.S. military was that of Private Eddie Slovik in 1945 , after a court-martial convicted him of desertion during World War II .

Hasan, a former Army major and psychiatrist, opened fire at Fort Hood on November 5, 2009 , killing 13 people and wounding 32 others while shouting “Allahu akbar,” which means “ God is great” in Arabic . He was convicted of premeditated murder in 2013 through the military justice system and sentenced to death. He is currently on military death row at Fort Leavenworth, Kansas.

Hasan was paralyzed from the waist down after being shot during the attack. He later told a panel of military mental health professionals that he wished he had been killed because it would have made him a martyr for his cause. He also said that if he were executed, he would still be considered a martyr.

NBC News reported this week that the idea of using a firing squad began taking shape inside the Pentagon earlier this year, according to two U.S. officials familiar with the planning. Sean Parnell , the Pentagon’s chief spokesperson, said on social media that President Donald Trump recently approved Hegseth’s recommendation to carry out the execution.

During the interview, Hegseth was asked whether he knew if Hasan had contacted Trump or made any final requests.

“Don’t care,” Hegseth said. “We’ll see him on Dec. 3rd.”

According to the Death Penalty Information Center , once a president approves a death sentence handed down by a military court, the service member can seek habeas corpus relief through the federal court system.

If that petition is denied, the service member would be escorted from death row to the execution chamber at the United States Disciplinary Barracks. Traditionally, the prisoner would be strapped to a gurney and executed by lethal injection. However, the Defense Department has said Hasan will be executed by firing squad.

Hasan has represented himself throughout the lengthy legal process, although two attorneys from the U.S. Army Trial Defense Service have assisted him as needed. It remains unclear whether he will appeal the method of execution.

articles.title: Who is eligible to get their benefits adjusted for next year with the COLA Increase 2027?
articles.standfirst: Millions of Americans could receive higher monthly payments in 2027 as Social Security prepares to announce its annual inflation adjustment
articles.summary: Millions of Americans could receive higher monthly payments in 2027 as Social Security prepares to announce its annual inflation adjustment
articles.body:
Millions of Americans who rely on government benefits are preparing for the next annual cost-of-living adjustment, commonly known as COLA .

The increase is designed to help Social Security recipients maintain some of their purchasing power as prices for everyday necessities, including food, housing and healthcare, rise.

The adjustment is not limited to people who have retired. It also applies to eligible beneficiaries receiving Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) , survivor benefits and Supplemental Security Income (SSI) .

The amount each person receives will depend on their existing benefit and the rules governing their particular program.

As of October 9, 2026, the Social Security Administration (SSA) has not confirmed the final COLA for 2027. The Senior Citizens League, an advocacy organization that tracks Social Security benefits, projected a 3.5% increase in September.

That would be higher than the 2.8% adjustment that took effect in 2026, although the final figure depends on the relevant inflation data.

Which beneficiaries qualify for the 2027 COLA increase?

The adjustment generally applies automatically to people already receiving eligible Social Security benefits. Recipients do not need to submit a separate application simply to receive the annual COLA .

Retired workers are among the largest groups affected. Whether someone retired at full retirement age, claimed benefits early or waited beyond full retirement age, their existing Social Security retirement benefit is adjusted when a COLA is implemented.

People receiving Social Security Disability Insurance can also qualify. SSDI provides benefits to eligible workers whose qualifying disabilities prevent them from maintaining substantial employment, subject to the program's medical and work-history requirements.

The COLA adjusts eligible payments under the same annual framework used for other Social Security benefits.

Survivors may also benefit. Social Security provides payments to eligible family members of deceased workers, including qualifying widows, widowers and children. When those payments are eligible for the annual adjustment, recipients can see their monthly benefits increase as well.

Spouses and qualifying dependents receiving benefits based on another worker's earnings record may also be covered. Eligibility depends on the type of benefit being paid, rather than simply on whether someone is related to a Social Security recipient.

Supplemental Security Income is another important category. Unlike standard Social Security retirement and disability insurance, SSI is a needs-based program for people who meet its income and resource requirements and are aged 65 or older, blind or disabled.
